b2-semmelweis-01.title: Communicative Challenge: Hands in the Vienna Clinic
b2-semmelweis-01.scenario: At a history evening in Budapest, a guest named Judit asks you how Semmelweis worked out why so many mothers died in the Vienna hospital.
b2-semmelweis-01.prompt: Tell Judit what shocked Semmelweis in 1847 and what he ordered.
cues: Say what the doctors should not have done after the autopsies
Say what he had them do in the clinic
b2-semmelweis-01.target: Az orvosoknak nem lett volna szabad fertőtlenítés nélkül a boncteremből a szülőszobába menniük. Semmelweis ezért 1847 májusában elrendelte, hogy mindenkinek klórvízben kell kezet mosnia.
b2-semmelweis-01.english: The doctors should not have gone from the autopsy room into the delivery room without disinfection. So in May 1847 Semmelweis ordered that everyone must wash their hands in chlorine water.
b2-semmelweis-01.canDo: I can recount how Ignác Semmelweis linked childbed fever to doctors' hands in Vienna in 1847.

b2-semmelweis-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Why They Would Not Listen
b2-semmelweis-02.scenario: At a medical students' evening in Pest, a student named Márk asks you why the Vienna doctors did not accept Semmelweis's results.
b2-semmelweis-02.prompt: Tell Márk what made it hard for the doctors and what Semmelweis could have done differently.
cues: Say what thought many chief physicians found hard to face
Say what Semmelweis put off for more than ten years
b2-semmelweis-02.target: Sok főorvos nehezen nézett szembe a gondolattal, hogy a rájuk bízott betegek az ő mulasztásuk miatt haltak meg. Semmelweis több mint tíz évig nem jelentette meg a könyvét, pedig könnyebben meggyőzhette volna a kétkedőket.
b2-semmelweis-02.english: Many chief physicians found it hard to face the thought that the patients entrusted to them had died because of their negligence. Semmelweis did not publish his book for more than ten years, although he could have convinced the doubters more easily.
b2-semmelweis-02.canDo: I can discuss some reasons why many 19th-century physicians rejected Semmelweis's evidence, and what the 'Semmelweis reflex' means.

b2-semmelweis-03.title: Communicative Challenge: The Paprika Evening
b2-semmelweis-03.scenario: In a school in Szeged, a teacher named Gabriella asks you how Szeged paprika helped Albert Szent-Györgyi win a Nobel Prize.
b2-semmelweis-03.prompt: Tell Gabriella what the paprika made possible and what Szent-Györgyi received in 1937.
cues: Say what he could not have done in a week without the Szeged paprika
Say which prize he received in 1937
b2-semmelweis-03.target: A szegedi paprika nélkül Szent-Györgyi nem tudott volna egy hét alatt több kilónyi aszkorbinsavat kivonni. 1937-ben orvosi-élettani Nobel-díjat kapott.
b2-semmelweis-03.english: Without the Szeged paprika, Szent-Györgyi could not have extracted several kilos of ascorbic acid in a week. In 1937 he received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
b2-semmelweis-03.canDo: I can narrate how Albert Szent-Györgyi's research in Szeged on paprika and vitamin C led to the 1937 Nobel Prize.

b2-semmelweis-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Perseverance in the Laboratory
b2-semmelweis-04.scenario: At a research institute in Szeged, a young researcher named Tamás asks you how Katalin Karikó kept going after the university demoted her.
b2-semmelweis-04.prompt: Tell Tamás what Karikó chose in 1995 and what she received in 2023.
cues: Say what other researchers could have done in her place
Say what she chose instead of rank
Say which prize she received in 2023
b2-semmelweis-04.target: Sok más kutató feladhatta volna az álmát, Karikó azonban a laboratóriumi munkát választotta a rang helyett. 2023-ban Drew Weissmannal együtt átvehette az orvosi-élettani Nobel-díjat.
b2-semmelweis-04.english: Many other researchers could have given up their dream, but Karikó chose laboratory work instead of rank. In 2023 she and Drew Weissman received the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
b2-semmelweis-04.canDo: I can trace Katalin Karikó's journey from Szeged to the University of Pennsylvania and the 2023 Nobel Prize.

b2-semmelweis-05.title: Communicative Challenge: What the Three Stories Teach
b2-semmelweis-05.scenario: At a seminar on science and trust, a lecturer named Dr Szabó asks you what the institutions should have done in the stories of Semmelweis and Karikó.
b2-semmelweis-05.prompt: Tell Dr Szabó what the clinic directors and the reviewers should have done.
cues: Say what the nineteenth-century clinic directors should have set aside
Say what the reviewers should have seen about unsuccessful experiments
b2-semmelweis-05.target: A tizenkilencedik századi klinikaigazgatóknak félre kellett volna tenniük a hiúságukat, és el kellett volna rendelniük a fertőtlenítést. A bírálóknak látniuk kellett volna, hogy a látszólag sikertelen kísérletek is értékes tudást halmoznak fel.
b2-semmelweis-05.english: The nineteenth-century clinic directors should have set aside their vanity and ordered disinfection. The reviewers should have seen that even seemingly unsuccessful experiments accumulate valuable knowledge.
b2-semmelweis-05.canDo: I can compare the historical trajectories of Semmelweis, Szent-Györgyi, and Karikó regarding institutional trust and peer review.

b2-semmelweis-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: Three Pioneers, One Evening
b2-semmelweis-consolidation.scenario: At the end of a school project, a teacher, Mrs Kiss, asks you to say what each of the three Hungarian pioneers is known for.
b2-semmelweis-consolidation.prompt: Tell Mrs Kiss what could have been prevented in Vienna and what Szent-Györgyi and Karikó achieved.
cues: Say what could have been saved by handwashing
Say what Szent-Györgyi extracted from paprika
b2-semmelweis-consolidation.target: Édesanyák ezreit meg lehetett volna menteni a klórvizes kézmosással. Szent-Györgyi a szegedi paprikából vonta ki a C-vitamint, Karikó pedig kitartott az mRNS-kutatás mellett.
b2-semmelweis-consolidation.english: The lives of thousands of mothers could have been saved with chlorinated handwashing. Szent-Györgyi extracted vitamin C from Szeged paprika, and Karikó stuck with mRNA research.
b2-semmelweis-consolidation.canDo: I can discuss the breakthroughs and institutional struggles of Ignác Semmelweis, Albert Szent-Györgyi, and Katalin Karikó.
